verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the root cause the same way. Each maps the CRM `customer_id` to `customerId` at load time and switches the export to `requireCustomer`, so behavior is effectively identical. B is slightly better in three ways. It extracts a small named `fromCrm` helper and keeps the original list structure. Its sources test builds an isolated temp fixture and checks the merged order, instead of depending on the live `data/` files. Its export test uses `instanceof UnknownReferenceError`, as the existing tests do. Both reports are accurate, and B adds hand-checked totals.
a_issues: tests/sources.test.js reads the real `data/` directory, which couples the test to production data files and the working directory.
The unknown-customer test checks `error.name` as a string rather than `instanceof UnknownReferenceError`, which differs from the existing test style.
The inlined destructuring map makes `loadCustomerRecords` a bit denser and reorders the file reads (CRM before billing) for no reason.
b_issues: The import order in tests/export.test.js puts errors.js before customers.js, a trivial inconsistency.

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same fix: they map the CRM `customer_id` to `customerId` at load time and switch the export to `requireCustomer`, so behavior is effectively identical. A puts the mapping in a small named `fromCrm` helper and tests `loadCustomerRecords` against its own temporary fixture files. B's sources test reads the real `data/` directory relative to the working directory, which ties the test to production data that changes monthly. A's report has a typo but is otherwise accurate; B's report explains the CLI exit behavior well but mentions an extra `/tmp` write.
a_issues: In tests/export.test.js the errors.js import is placed before customers.js, breaking the alphabetical import order the file otherwise follows.
b_issues: tests/sources.test.js reads the real `data/` directory relative to the working directory, so it breaks if the monthly data changes or the tests run from another directory.
The CRM mapping is an inline lambda in the loader, which reads less clearly than a named helper; the CRM file is now read before the billing file, a small needless reorder.
The unknown-customer test checks `error.name` instead of `instanceof UnknownReferenceError`, which is weaker than the existing tests in the repo.
Wrote an extra output file to /tmp/invoices.csv, which nobody asked for.
